concepts.def: Northwest and west: older, harder rocks (granite, slate); higher relief; e.g. Scottish Highlands, Lake District, Snowdonia.
Southeast: younger, softer sedimentary rocks (chalk, clay); flatter relief; e.g. London Basin, East Anglia.
Diagonal line dividing UK between upland west/north and lowland south/east; reflects geological boundary.
Last Ice Age (until c.10,000 years ago) shaped uplands with U-shaped valleys, corries, ribbon lakes.
UK's 17,820km coast includes rocky (Cornwall), chalk (Dover), sandy (East Anglia), estuarine (Severn).
Major rivers (Thames, Severn, Trent) flow from uplands to lowlands; demonstrate upper, middle, lower course features.
